items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: Bo Diddley, you name it, there was a cafe in my neighborhood under the hill that these guys used to come weekly.

ctx.x: Those things just stay in your consciousness, don’t they?

Oh yeah. They are the roots. You know every tree has a root, right? They’re the roots. They’re the branches. Those are the roots of your branch of your life. Those are things that people don’t see or don’t know. Those are things that focus your soul. And all of these things is what you branch out and you grow into a tree and what-have-you, and bear fruit and what-have-you. But the roots are of those things that my mother planted in me. And I have to go through this real briefly. My mother brought me up in the…

Christmas plays, and I was just in love with music from that state. Then on the other side in my neighborhood B.B. King, Howlin’ Wolf, Muddy Waters, Bo Diddley, you name it, there was a cafe in my neighborhood under the hill that these guys used to come weekly. Every week it was either Muddy Waters was there, B.B. was there, and Howlin’ Wolf would be there the next week, and oh just — had some local guys that there was always music on the weekend.
